canonical_definition: Multimodal Understanding refers to the capability of models to jointly process, integrate, and reason over information from multiple modalities—primarily vision and language, but also including audio, video, tables, equations, or 3D data—within a unified semantic framework. This construct emphasizes cross-modal alignment, where inputs from different modalities are encoded into shared representations to enable tasks requiring contextual comprehension, such as answering questions, generating responses, or making decisions that depend on inter-modal relationships. While some definitions focus narrowly on vision-text integration, others extend to broader multimodal combinations, with consensus on the necessity of joint processing rather than isolated unimodal analysis.
